questions: Is the reversal operation a global toggle (all edges reverse direction each time it's used) or a one-time permanent reversal?
Can the reversal operation be used multiple times, and if so, does the graph revert to original after two reversals?
Is the cost X incurred each time the reversal operation is performed, regardless of whether it changes reachable paths?
Are self-loops (u_i = v_i) allowed, and if so, how do they behave under reversal?
When moving along a directed edge, must the edge exist in the current orientation of the graph at that moment?
Is the goal to minimize total cost, or is there a unique deterministic sequence implied?
Can we reverse edges even if we are at vertex N (already reached), or does process stop immediately upon reaching N?
Does the reversal affect all edges simultaneously, including those not incident to current vertex?
